fullDescription:
A catamaran rather than a longtail, which changes what the four islands feel like more than you would expect.

The power catamaran has two decks, real shade and open-air seating, and it does not pound through chop the way a speedboat does or soak everyone the way a longtail does when the sea picks up. For an evening cruise that matters: you are on board for four hours, most of it sitting, and the boat is the thing you actually spend the time on.

The route runs out around Poda, Chicken Island and the Thale Waek sandbar area, with a swim stop in the shallow turquoise water between them. Snorkelling equipment is on board for anyone who wants it, though at this hour the point is the swim more than the reef.

Sunset over the Krabi coastline is the reason the trip runs late. The limestone karsts hold colour for a long time after the sun has gone, turning from orange to a deep red-grey, and from the water you get the whole ridge line rather than a slice of it through a gap in the trees. Thai snacks and drinks are served as the light goes.

This is the version to book if you want the islands without a full day of getting in and out of boats, or if someone in the group is not confident on a small craft.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the catamaran cruise with crew, an English-speaking host, Thai snacks, soft drinks and water, snorkelling equipment, life jackets and insurance.

Four hours from Ao Nang, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Two-deck power catamaran with shade and open seating
Steadier than a speedboat, drier than a longtail
Swim stop in shallow water between the islands
Sunset along the full Krabi karst ridge
Thai snacks, drinks and snorkel gear on board

fullDescription:
The seven-island route run as an evening trip, with dinner cooked on the boat and a plankton swim to finish.

The islands off Ao Nang are busy from mid-morning to mid-afternoon and then empty out almost completely. Leaving in the afternoon means arriving at the later stops after the day fleet has turned for home, so the beaches you see in the last two hours are not the same beaches the morning boats saw.

Snorkelling happens while there is light, over shallow reef the guide picks on the day according to the water. Sunset is taken from the boat somewhere among the islands, and the barbecue dinner is served after dark.

The plankton swim is the last stop. The light comes from dinoflagellates that flash when the water around them moves, so it appears as sparks around your hands and feet rather than a glow across the surface. It is not guaranteed on any given night. A dark sky near the new moon gives the strongest display, a full moon effectively erases it, and choppy water scatters it. Ask about the moon phase before you fix a date if this is the part you care about.

Seven hours from pickup to drop-off, so expect a full evening.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers round-trip transfer from Krabi Town or Ao Nang, barbecue dinner with drinking water and fruit, life jacket, snorkelling mask, tour guide, first aid kit and accident insurance.

Bring a towel, dry clothes and something warm for the ride back. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Afternoon start, so the late stops are near-empty
Snorkelling in daylight, barbecue dinner after dark
Sunset from the water among the islands
Plankton swim, strongest on dark nights near a new moon
Transfers, dinner, guide and snorkel gear included

fullDescription:
A pre-dawn start that buys you the two things every Phi Phi day trip is short of: an empty Maya Bay and an empty beach to eat breakfast on.

The speedboat leaves before first light and runs to Poda Island while the tour fleet is still loading in Ao Nang. Breakfast is a picnic on the sand with the island effectively to yourselves, which is the opposite of how Poda looks at eleven in the morning when a dozen boats are moored off it.

Maya Bay comes next, and timing is the whole point. The bay was closed completely from 2018 to 2022 to let the reef recover and reopened under strict rules: boats moor at the back of Phi Phi Leh and visitors walk in through the island, swimming inside the bay is restricted, and daily numbers are capped. Arriving first means walking in before the queue forms rather than after.

Pileh Lagoon follows, a channel of deep green water enclosed by cliffs on all sides, and snorkelling stops are chosen around Phi Phi according to conditions. Lunch is on the boat or on a beach depending on the day.

Eleven hours including an early pickup makes this a long day and the early start is not negotiable, since being ahead of the fleet is the entire value of the trip.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers early hotel pickup and drop-off, the speedboat with crew, an English-speaking guide, picnic breakfast on the beach, lunch, snorkelling equipment, drinking water, fruit and life jackets.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Pre-dawn departure, ahead of the whole tour fleet
Picnic breakfast on a near-empty Poda Island
Maya Bay before the day boats arrive
Pileh Lagoon, enclosed by cliffs on every side
Speedboat, guide, breakfast and lunch included

fullDescription:
Eight hours covering the seven-island route from the middle of the day through to after dark, so you get both halves of it.

The longer version starts early enough to include lunch and late enough to finish with the plankton, which means you see the islands busy and then see them empty. That contrast is the argument for the eight-hour trip over the shorter evening ones: the same beaches behave completely differently once the day fleet leaves.

Snorkelling stops are chosen on the day. Krabi's reef sits shallow and close to the islands, and which stop is worth using depends on the tide and how much the wind has stirred the water, so a fixed list would be a fiction. The guide picks.

Sunset is taken from the boat. The limestone holds colour well after the sun is down, which is why the light here lasts longer than the clock suggests.

The plankton swim closes the trip. Dinoflagellates flash when disturbed, so the light appears around your hands and feet as you move. It genuinely depends on the night: dark skies near a new moon give the best display, a full moon washes it out, and rough water scatters it. Treat it as the likely highlight rather than a guarantee.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers lunch, drinking water, fruit, hotel transfer, tour guide, insurance, snorkelling mask and life jacket.

Eight hours, bring a towel and dry clothes for the ride back. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Eight hours: the islands busy, then the islands empty
Lunch included, plankton swim to finish
Snorkelling stops picked on the day for conditions
Sunset from the water over the limestone
Transfers, guide, mask and life jacket included

fullDescription:
The four-island route plus Railay, in five and a half hours rather than a full day.

Railay is the addition that makes this different from the standard circuit. The peninsula has no road access at all, cut off by limestone headlands, so every visitor arrives by boat. Phra Nang Cave Beach at its southern end is the reason to go: a stretch of sand under an overhanging cliff with the cave shrine at one end, where fishermen leave carved wooden offerings to a spirit they believe protects them at sea. The offerings are unmistakable and the shrine is still actively used, so it is worth being unobtrusive about photographs.

The island stops cover Poda, Tup and the Thale Waek sandbar area. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is a strip of sand that links islands at low tide and disappears entirely at high tide, which is why departure timing follows the tide table rather than a fixed clock.

Lunch is a mini Thai buffet served on Poda.

At five and a half hours this sits between the quick sunset trips and the full-day circuits. It suits people who want the main sights without spending the whole day on a boat, and families who would find eight hours too long.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers pickup from Ao Nang or Ao Nam Mao, the boat tour, Phra Nang Cave Beach at Railay, Poda Island with the buffet lunch, and the other island stops.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Railay, reachable only by boat, plus the four islands
Phra Nang Cave Beach and its working fishermen's shrine
Thale Waek sandbar, timed to the tide
Thai buffet lunch served on Poda Island
Five and a half hours, shorter than a full day circuit

fullDescription:
The four-island circuit run late in the day by a community-based operator, finishing with sunset at Phra Nang.

Most boats do this route in the morning. Going in the afternoon means arriving at each stop as the day fleet is leaving, so Koh Poda and Chicken Island are quiet by the time you get there rather than lined with moored boats.

Chicken Island takes its name from the rock formation at its tip, which reads as a chicken's head from one particular angle on the approach and as an ordinary limestone stack from everywhere else. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is the sandbar that emerges at low tide and links the islands into a walkable strip, then disappears again as the tide comes in. Whether you can walk it depends entirely on when you are there, which is why the timing follows the tide table.

Sunset is taken at Phra Nang Cave Beach on the Railay peninsula. The cliff behind the beach catches the last light, and the cave shrine at the end of the sand is where fishermen leave carved offerings to a spirit believed to protect them at sea.

The guide is local and community-based rather than employed by a large boat company, which in practice means the commentary is about the place and the fishing rather than a script.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers visits to Koh Poda, Chicken Island and Thale Waek, sunset at Phra Nang Cave, and a local guide.

Six hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Afternoon route, so each stop is emptying out
Thale Waek sandbar, walkable only at low tide
Sunset at Phra Nang Cave Beach on Railay
The fishermen's shrine, still actively used
Local community-based guide rather than a boat company
